anchors.statement: omega^2 = g k tanh(kh) for linear surface gravity waves of wavenumber k in still-water depth h
anchors.source: H. Lamb, Hydrodynamics, 6th ed., Cambridge UP (1932), art. 228; G. B. Airy (1845) for the finite-depth form
anchors.how_used: closed-form reference evaluated at h = 1 m, g = 9.80665 m/s^2, kh in [0.1, 5]; the criterion is the relative error of the numerical operator's omega against this expression

anchors.statement: Boussinesq / Green-Naghdi class models replace tanh(x)/x by a rational approximation; the [6/6] Pade is the member that stays within a few percent up to kh = O(5)
anchors.source: J. Boussinesq (1872); A. E. Green & N. A. Naghdi, J. Fluid Mech. 78 (1976) 237; Pade table of tanh (Baker & Graves-Morris, 1996)
anchors.how_used: the operator's own symbol is compared with the Pade expressions in tensordg/dispersive.py (model_dispersion_error); the low-kh members (boussinesq, pade22) are reported with their measured validity limit instead of being averaged away

anchors.statement: the time-reversing deformational flow with cos(pi t/T) returns the initial field exactly at T, so the final-time L2 error is a pure measure of numerical dissipation incurred on unresolved filaments
anchors.source: R. J. LeVeque, 'High-resolution conservative algorithms for advection', SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 33 (1996) 627-665; test 2 of the deformational-flow suite
anchors.how_used: defines the velocity field and the exact-recovery reference at T

anchors.statement: the KdV equation has the exact travelling solution eta = a sech^2((x - ct)/w), w = sqrt(4 h^3/(3a)), c = sqrt(gh)(1 + a/(2h)); its amplitude never decays
anchors.source: D. J. Korteweg & G. de Vries (1895); N. J. Zabusky & M. D. Kruskal, Phys. Rev. Lett. 15 (1965) 240; P. G. Drazin & R. S. Johnson, Solitons: an Introduction, Cambridge UP (1989), ch. 3
anchors.how_used: reference profile after a propagation of 10 soliton widths; the measured celerity is compared both with the KdV value and with the shallow-water form sqrt(g(h+a)) requested by the campaign

anchors.statement: under solid-body rotation the exact solution is the initial field rigidly rotated by -omega T; for T = 2 pi/omega it is the initial field itself
anchors.source: standard advection-verification anchor (e.g. W. J. Rider & L. G. Margolin, 'Revisiting wall heating', J. Comput. Phys. 162 (2000) 395, rigid-rotation test)
anchors.how_used: the reference field is built by rotating the coordinates back, independently of the solver's coefficient update
